questions.question: A project sets a saved `storageState`. Which line makes a group of tests start signed out?
options: `test.use({ storageState: undefined })`
`test.use({ storageState: { cookies: [], origins: [] } })`
`test.use({ storageState: null, baseURL: undefined })`
`test.use({ contextOptions: { clean: true } })`
questions.explanation: The empty state replaces the project's login. With `undefined`, the project's saved session stayed in force and the private page still opened.

questions.question: An app keeps its login token in `sessionStorage`. What happens after you save and reuse `storageState`?
options: The token is restored with the cookies
Playwright stops with an error when saving
The token is missing, so the user starts signed out
The token is moved into `localStorage`

questions.question: Three parallel tests share one saved customer login. Each adds a product and expects a cart quantity of 1. What is the likely result?
options: Some fail, because they all change the same server-side cart
All pass, because each test has its own browser context
All are skipped by the setup project
Playwright runs them one at a time because they share a login
questions.explanation: Contexts isolate the browser, not the account on the server. Give each test that changes server data its own user.

questions.question: Why does the factory build emails with `randomUUID()` instead of `faker.internet.email()`?
options: Faker can't generate email addresses
Faker's emails are rejected by every browser
A UUID makes the test run faster
Faker's values are realistic but can repeat
questions.explanation: In 10,000 calls, `faker.internet.email()` produced 11 duplicates. Anything the app requires to be unique needs a unique part.

questions.question: A config has `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`, and someone runs the suite locally with `CI=false`. A `test.only` is in the code. What happens?
options: Only the focused test runs
The run stops, because the string 'false' is truthy
All tests run and `test.only` is ignored
The focused test is skipped
questions.explanation: `!!'false'` is `true`, because any non-empty string is truthy, so `forbidOnly` is on and the run reports an error.
